# Ensure every Main Street card has dedicated card art (1024×1024 source)

## Problem statement

Every Main Street card renders a square art zone in its top-left corner, but
**108 of the 171 unique cards in `card-data.csv` currently render the same
generic `Fallback` sprite**, so the bulk of the deck is visually
indistinguishable. A player cannot tell an `Upgrade to Patisserie` from a
`Chef` from a `Rainy Day` at a glance, which undermines the 64×64 left-art
redesign's whole purpose.

## Users

- **Player (market / hand / street):** needs to recognise a card by its art
  without reading the title — especially when cards overlap in hand or stack
  on the street.
- **Content author:** needs a documented, testable rule for what art a card
  resolves to, so new cards cannot silently reintroduce `Fallback` art.
- **Engine maintainer:** needs one art-resolution path shared by the runtime
  generator and the static SVG exporter, guarded by a regression test.

User stories:

- As a player, when I look at the market, I can tell any two cards apart by
  their art alone.
- As an upgrade card, I show the art of the business I enhance under my new
  display name, so my purpose is obvious.
- As a content author, when I add a card to `card-data.csv`, the test suite
  tells me if I forgot to give it art.

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-26)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q1 | Art scope / strategy | **Option A — reuse-first.** Actively **duplicate the existing art under the new (card/display) name**, and produce **new art only where necessary** (no suitable existing art). |
| Q2 | Art production ownership | **The producer will produce the new sprites.** This item still owns the mapping, resolver, regeneration tooling and the drift guard. |
| Q3 | Event mapping granularity | **Map events by `trigger` × `targetSynergy` category** (a documented, generated mapping). |

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-29)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q4 | Source-art size | The producer provides **1024×1024** source art (`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`). The “64×64” is the on-card display zone, not the production size. |
| Q5 | Staff art granularity | **One sprite per staff role** (24 sprites). |
| Q6 | Event-category art | **Unique (bespoke) sprite per `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category** — representatives are not reused. |
| Q7 | Drift-guard tightening | **Yes** — tighten the guard to a strict “zero `Fallback` for every card in `card-data.csv`” assertion once the sprites land, in the same change. |
| Q8 | Duplicate-name clash | **Rename to remove the clashes**: business `Florist` → `Flower Shop`; event `Community Garden` → `Garden Party`. |

Art-production ownership (Q2, 2026-09-26) is unchanged: the producer supplies
all new source sprites.

## Existing state (verified 2026-09-26, `dev` @ 933644bc)

Resolution path (all four card families call it with the card's `name`):

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` → `resolveCardArtName()` /
  `hasDedicatedCardArt()`: (1) spelling alias → (2) exact name → (3)
  `Fallback`.
- Map built by `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs`
  from committed `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` files into
  `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json`.
- A second consumer, `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`,
  duplicates the alias/lookup logic and must be kept in step.

Verified counts:

- `card-data.csv`: **173 rows / 171 unique names** (duplicate names across
  families: `Florist` = business + staff, `Community Garden` = community-space
  + event → name-keyed resolution shares one sprite).
- Committed sprites: **62 dedicated + `Fallback`** (63 map entries).
- Cards resolving today: **65** (63 exact + 2 via aliases).
- **Cards rendering `Fallback`: 108**:

| Family              | Cards | Resolving | Missing |
|---------------------|------:|----------:|--------:|
| business            |    30 |        28 |       2 |
| community-space     |     8 |         1 |       7 |
| upgrade             |    39 |         0 |      39 |
| staff               |    25 |         1 |      24 |
| event               |    71 |        35 |      36 |
| **Total**           |  **173** | **65** | **108** |

Every missing card already has an `art_notes` description in `card-data.csv`
(the source the existing 1024×1024 sprites were built from). There is **no
in-repo image generator** — the existing sprites were committed out-of-band
(commit `05026750`), and the producer will continue producing new art the same
way.

## Size clarification (reviewed 2026-09-29)

The “64×64” in the original title is the **on-card display zone** — a layout
dimension in SVG user units — **not** the size of the source art to produce.
Code review of the generator and renderer confirms three distinct layers:

| Layer | Size | Where | Role |
|-------|-----:|-------|------|
| On-card art zone | 64×64 | `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` (`GRAPHIC_*`) | SVG layout box only |
| Embedded bitmap | 256×256 | `src/card-art-map.json` (`artResolution`) | WebP `data:` URI in the SVG |
| **Source art** | **1024×1024** | `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` | Generator input |

`src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` only loads files named
`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` (`SOURCE_SUFFIX = '_1024_x_1024.png'`) and downscales
each to 256×256 WebP (`ART_RESOLUTION = 256`). Phaser rasterises the card SVG
at `qualityScale = max(4, dpr)`, so the 64×64 zone needs a ≥256×256 bitmap to
stay crisp; a 64×64 source would be stretched ~4× and appear pixelated.

**Produce every new sprite at 1024×1024**, named `<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`, in
`src/sprites/`. The legacy `<Name>_64_x_64.png` files are superseded
thumbnails and are not read by the generator.

## Progress (2026-09-29)

The mapping/resolver/tooling + pending-aware drift guard landed on `dev` as
commit `4b80741` (full unit suite green): `src/card-art-map.json` is now
`version: 3`. Real coverage rose from **65 → 95 of 171** unique cards.

**Duplicate names split (commit `874f419`).** On producer decision Q8 the two
duplicate card names were renamed, so all **173 card names are now unique**:

- business `Florist` → **`Flower Shop`** — keeps the existing rose sprite
  (renamed `Flower Shop_1024_x_1024.png`); its `upgradePath` and
  `Upgrade to Garden Center`'s `targetBusiness` both follow.
- event `Community Garden` → **`Garden Party`** — now needs its own art and maps
  to the `Investment__` category until then.
- staff `Florist` keeps its name; its business restriction is now
  `Flower Shop|Commerce|Culture`.

Card IDs are intentionally unchanged (`biz-florist`, `evt-community-garden`) to
preserve save/challenge compatibility. After the split, **95 of 173** cards
resolve and **78** still render `Fallback`: the staff `Florist` and event
`Garden Party` joined the pending set, giving **46 distinct source sprites** to
produce.

## Desired change (confirmed strategy)

1. **Upgrades (39) — duplicate target art under the new display name.**
   For each `Upgrade to …`, copy the art of its `targetBusiness` to a new
   source sprite named after the upgrade's `newDisplayName` (all 39 are
   distinct, no collisions, and none is already a sprite). Seven targets are
   themselves gaps, so their art must be produced first: `Cafe`,
   `Health Kiosk`, `Laundromat`, `Library`, `Park`, `Playground`,
   `Town Fountain`.
2. **Business / community-space gaps (9) — new art.** `Laundromat`, `Cafe` and
   all community spaces except `Community Garden`: `Park`, `Library`,
   `Playground`, `Town Fountain`, `Health Kiosk`, `Community Shelter`,
   `Public Art`.
3. **Staff (25) — new staff art.** **One sprite per staff role** (confirmed
   2026-09-29), produced by the producer. The split moved `Florist` (staff)
   off the shared business sprite, so all 25 roles need art.
4. **Events (37) — category mapping.** Map each event to a category sprite
   keyed by `(trigger, targetSynergy)`; **unique (bespoke) art per category**
   (confirmed 2026-09-29), produced by the producer. `Garden Party` joined the
   category-mapped set after the split.
5. **Resolver / map.** Extend the generated mapping (and/or `CARD_ART_ALIASES`)
   so both consumers agree and regeneration stays deterministic; keep
   `Fallback` only as the genuine last resort.
6. **Drift guard.** Add a unit test over `card-data.csv` asserting full
   coverage and failing when a new art-less card appears.

## Required art (derived)

| Group | Cards | Mechanism | New sprites |
|-------|------:|-----------|------------:|
| Upgrade | 39 | Duplicate `targetBusiness` art under each upgrade's `newDisplayName` | 0 new (39 copies) |
| Business + community-space gaps | 9 | New source art | 9 |
| Staff | 25 | New source art — one per role | 25 |
| Event | 37 | Unique `(trigger × targetSynergy)` category art — 12 categories | 12 |
| **Total distinct source sprites** | | | **46** |

Event categories for the 36 missing events (representative = an event with
dedicated art today in the same category, available to duplicate):

| `trigger` | `targetSynergy` | Cards | Existing representative |
|-----------|-----------------|------:|-------------------------|
| Incident  | (none)          | 9 | Tax Audit |
| Incident  | Culture         | 1 | Cultural Grant |
| Incident  | Entertainment   | 1 | Noise Complaint |
| Incident  | Food            | 6 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Health          | 1 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Service         | 4 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| (none)          | 3 | Charity Drive |
| Investment| Commerce        | 1 | Grand Opening Sale |
| Investment| Entertainment   | 3 | Street Performer |
| Investment| Food            | 2 | Harvest Festival |
| Investment| Health          | 3 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| Service         | 2 | *(none — new)* |

Existing dedicated event art (35 events) is retained; only the 36 missing
events are category-mapped. **The producer confirmed on 2026-09-29 that each of
the 12 categories gets unique (bespoke) art** — the “existing representative”
column above is informational only and is not reused.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every **unique** card name in `card-data.csv` resolves via
   `MainStreetCardArt.hasDedicatedCardArt()` to a **non-`Fallback`** sprite
   (documented alias/category mapping counts); currently 65/171.
2. All 39 upgrade cards resolve to art duplicated from their `targetBusiness`
   under the upgrade's `newDisplayName`; no upgrade renders `Fallback`.
3. All 24 staff cards resolve to dedicated staff art; no staff card renders
   `Fallback`.
4. All 36 missing event cards resolve to a documented
   `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category sprite; no event card renders `Fallback`.
5. All 9 business / community-space gaps resolve to dedicated art; no card in
   either family renders `Fallback`.
6. A unit-test drift guard over `card-data.csv` asserts AC 1–5 and fails when a
   new card is added without art; `Fallback` remains in the map and resolver for
   genuinely-unknown/future cards (the existing "unknown card" test still passes).
7. Both consumers of `card-art-map.json` (runtime `MainStreetCardArt.ts` and
   `scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`) apply the identical mapping;
   regeneration via `scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` is
   deterministic and reproducible.
8. `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` and `public/assets/CREDITS.md`
   document the mapping rules and the licence/attribution of any new art.
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
10. `npm run build` is green and the **full project test suite must pass** with
    the new changes.

## Constraints

- New art must be permissively licensed (CC0 / MIT / Apache 2.0) and attributed
  in `public/assets/CREDITS.md`.
- Source art remains `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`; `card-art-map.json`
  stays generated (never hand-edited).
- No change to the 64×64 zone geometry, the 140×80 card size, the 256×256
  embedded WebP format, or the SVG being self-contained (inline `data:` URI).
- Mapping logic must be expressed once and consumed by both the runtime and the
  static generator.

## Desired artefacts

- Up to 45 new `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` source files (9 business /
  community-space, 24 staff, up to 12 event categories) and 39 upgrade
  duplicates named by `newDisplayName`.
- Updated generated mapping + resolver.
- Drift-guard unit test in `tests/main-street/`.
- Docs + credits updates.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` — resolver: targetBusiness /
  category resolution or extended alias path.
- `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json` — regenerated mapping (data).
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` —
  derive the upgrade-duplication and event-category mapping from
  `card-data.csv` + sprites.
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` —
  second consumer; mirror the mapping.
- `example-games/main-street/sprites/` — new + duplicated `_1024_x_1024.png`
  source art (producer).
- `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` — add the `card-data.csv` drift guard.
- `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` — document mapping rules.
- `public/assets/CREDITS.md` — licence/attribution for new art.

## Risks / assumptions

- **Art-availability dependency:** the resolver/tooling can land independently,
  but AC 1–5 cannot pass until the producer's sprites are committed. Plan
  should sequence tooling + drift guard first, art last.
- **Duplicate-name collision (resolved 2026-09-29):** the business `Florist`
  and the event `Community Garden` were renamed to `Flower Shop` and
  `Garden Party` (Q8), so every card name is now unique and no sprite is shared
  across families. IDs are unchanged for save/challenge compatibility.
- **Category-art fidelity (resolved 2026-09-29):** the producer confirmed
  unique (bespoke) art for all 12 event categories, so no representative
  sprite is reused.
- **Dual-consumer drift risk:** `generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` duplicates
  the alias logic; a mapping change that misses it silently diverges — assert
  both in tests.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "improve the existing 62 sprites" and "redesign the art
  zone" are out of scope — record separately if they surface.
- **Assumption:** `hasDedicatedCardArt()` remains name-keyed; any targetBusiness
  indirection is baked into the generated map so the public API is unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Changing the 64×64 left-art geometry or the 140×80 card dimensions.
- New card types or `card-data.csv` content changes (beyond `art_notes` if new
  art needs them).
- Filling the empty gameplay `description` column on the 45 `event` rows
  (unrelated to art; all 173 rows already carry `art_notes`).
- Redesigning/replacing the existing 62 dedicated sprites.
- Adding an in-repo image-generation tool (the producer supplies the art).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 "Art scope / strategy: how much new art vs. mapping/reuse for the 108
  cards?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):** Option A — actively duplicate
  the current art using the new name; new art where necessary. Source:
  interactive producer reply.
- Q2 "Art production ownership & pipeline: who produces the new sprites, and
  does this item ship mapping machinery first?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-26):** "I will produce them." Source: interactive producer reply.
  Research: no in-repo sprite generator exists (last sprite commit
  `05026750`, external).
- Q3 "Event mapping granularity: what taxonomy, and is a category sprite
  acceptable for AC4?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):**
  `trigger` × `targetSynergy` categories. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q1 prior/open record superseded by the answers above (was OPEN QUESTION).
- Q4 "Source-art size: 64×64 or 1024×1024?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** the producer provides **1024×1024** source art; the 64×64 is
  the on-card display zone. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q5 "Staff art granularity: per-role or shared?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** **one sprite per role**. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q6 "Event-category art: reuse a representative or unique?" — **Answer
  (producer, 2026-09-29):** **unique** per category. Source: interactive
  producer reply.
- Q7 "Tighten the drift guard to strict zero-`Fallback` once art lands?" —
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-29):** **yes**. Source: interactive producer
  reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MP1QZC6Q005EMEZ** – Asset generation: placeholder SVGs for new cards (completed)
- **CG-0MLTFDAYD0J6KLY3** – Phaser Scene Static Card Layout (completed)
- **CG-0MPD5XALT007F1WV** – Gym Graphics: Card Flip Animation (DeckRng + HandPile) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: 0mtorj5fs006b0un, acceptance, add, alias, apache (+136 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — matched: acceptance, add, approach, art, asserts (+107 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: acceptance, add, alias, apache, approach (+104 more)

# Extend storyline options with conditional and cost-gated effects

## Problem statement

The generalised storyline option model (`StorylineOption`) currently supports
only a label, a single successor, and an apply/skip effect policy. Content and
engine authors cannot express options that are only available when the player
can afford them, that branch to different successors based on game state, or
that carry their own extra effects. The game-agnostic seam
(`src/MainStreetStoryline.ts`) was explicitly designed to grow into these
semantics, and this capability was deliberately deferred from the
`write-storylines` epic as speculative until now.

## Users

- **Engine/content authors** — need richer per-option semantics (affordability
  gates, state-based branching, extra effects) without bypassing the
  game-agnostic seam or hand-writing bespoke engine code per card.
- **TCE / Main Street developers** — need the extension to stay declarative,
  serialisable, statically validatable, and portable to the core engine.
- **Players** — should only be offered choices they can actually take, and
  should have their decisions reflected accurately in coins/reputation.
- **AI / Monte Carlo** — must keep selecting legal, presented options so
  headless games never stall or pick a hidden/unaffordable branch.

### Example user stories

- "As an engine author, I want to gate an option behind a coin/reputation cost,
  so the choice only appears when the player can afford it."
- "As a content designer, I want an option's successor to depend on coins or
  reputation, so one choice can lead down different branches."
- "As a content designer, I want an option to apply an extra effect on top of
  its apply/skip policy, so choices can have their own consequences."
- "As a developer, I want invalid cost/condition data to fail the validator, so
  mis-authored storylines cannot ship."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Backwards-compatible model extension.** `StorylineOption` gains optional
   `cost`, `extraEffect` (`{ coins?: number; reputation?: number }`), and
   ordered `conditionalSuccessors` (`{ when: { field: 'coins'|'reputation';
   op: '>='|'<='|'>'|'<'|'=='; value: number }; successorId }`) fields. Omitting
   all three preserves today's behaviour exactly — verified by the existing
   legacy-equivalence and C1 regression harness passing unchanged.
   *Metric: unit tests + existing regression harness pass with zero behavioural deltas.*

- **Cost gating.** An option whose `cost` exceeds the player's current
   coins/reputation is **omitted** from the presented option list; available
   options are computed and stored with the pending choice so resolution
   indexing, transcript tokens, and save/load stay stable. Selecting an
   affordable option deducts the declared cost as an additional payment,
   independent of its `effectPolicy`, and applies any `extraEffect`.
   *Metric: unit tests assert exact coin/reputation deltas, omission, and stable indexing.*

- **Conditional successors.** `conditionalSuccessors` is evaluated in order;
   the first matching rule wins, and the option's `successorId` is the fallback
   when none match. Above/below threshold, equality boundary, and no-match
   fallback cases are covered, including succeeding-card push.
   *Metric: unit tests for each boundary/fallback case.*

- **Static validation & schema.** The validator and manifest schema reject
   invalid new data — negative/empty cost, malformed conditions (unknown field
   or op, non-numeric value), and dangling conditional successors — while the
   shipped CSVs validate cleanly and the doc-drift test passes.
   *Metric: validator unit tests with broken fixtures + clean run on shipped content.*

- **AI / Monte Carlo integration.** `decideEventChoice` (and the generalised
   AI selection path) chooses only among presented/affordable options and
   accounts for cost/extra-effect deltas; the regression and Monte Carlo
   harnesses run to completion without stalls.
   *Metric: AI policy tests + regression/Monte Carlo harness green.*

- **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes — `docs/main-street/storylines.md` (option model, resolution
   lifecycle, roadmap), the migration notes in `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts`,
   and the CSV column reference in `src/README.md` (confirming the new
   semantics remain programmatic, not CSV-authored).
   *Metric: doc-drift test passes; reviewer confirms docs match code.*

- **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.
   *Metric: full test suite green.*

## Constraints

- **Programmatic authoring only (producer decision Q1=A).** Extend the
  in-memory model, engine resolution, validator, and schema. Keep the legacy
  CSV at the two-way Accept/Reject shape; do **not** add CSV columns for the
  new semantics.
- **Declarative and serialisable (producer decision Q3=A).** Only
  field/op/value conditions and numeric deltas. Arbitrary callbacks are out of
  scope here — see the follow-up work item below.
- **Game-agnostic seam.** New semantics must live behind
  `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` and keep the future core-engine extraction
  viable (pure/declarative data, no Main-Street globals baked in beyond the
  injected template registry).
- **Affordability is coins and/or reputation (producer decision Q2.1).** A cost
  may specify either or both; an option is available only when *all* specified
  costs are affordable.
- **Omit, do not disable (producer decision Q2.2).** Unaffordable options are
  removed from the presented list, not shown greyed out.
- **Cost is a real payment (producer decision Q2.3).** Deducted from the
  player in addition to the option's apply/skip effect policy.
- No shipped card content is expected to use the new semantics; existing
  gameplay must remain byte-for-byte equivalent.

## Existing state

- `StorylineOption` (`src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts`) = `{ label, successorId,
  effectPolicy }`. `CompiledStoryline` wraps an ordered option list.
- `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` compiles legacy `hasChoices` /
  `acceptNextCardId` / `rejectNextCardId` into `[Accept, Reject]`, and supports
  explicit multi-way lists via `registerStorylineOptions(eventId, options)`.
  `getStorylineOptions(event)` is pure (no state) and is used by callers,
  the validator, and the graph exporter.
- `resolveStorylineOption(state, event, option)`
  (`src/MainStreetStoryline.ts`) applies `effectPolicy` and pushes
  `option.successorId`; `resolveEventOption(state, optionIndex)`
  (`src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`) indexes the option list, records the
  transcript, and drives `pushChainCard`.
- `decideEventChoice` (`src/MainStreetEngineScoring.ts`) returns a binary
  `'accept' | 'reject'` and reasons about `coinDelta` / `reputationDelta`,
  `projectEventCoinDelta`, `eventSeverity`, and successor severity.
- Validation lives in `src/scripts/validate-storylines.ts`; the manifest/schema
  in `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` and
  `schemas/main-street-storyline.schema.json`; docs in
  `docs/main-street/storylines.md` (§2 model, §3 lifecycle, §9 seam, §10
  roadmap).
- `PendingEventChoice` (`src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts`) currently stores
  `{ event, chosenOption, resolved }`.

## Desired change

Extend the option model and resolution path so that:

1. Options declare an optional affordability `cost`; the presented option list
   is filtered to affordable options before the dialog/AI sees it, and the
   filtered list is stored with the pending choice.
2. Options declare an optional `extraEffect` and ordered
   `conditionalSuccessors`, both applied/selected at resolution time using the
   declarative predicate vocabulary.
3. Selection deducts `cost`, applies `extraEffect` independently of
   `effectPolicy`, and pushes the first matching conditional successor (or the
   default `successorId`).
4. The validator, schema, and graph/manifest export understand the new fields;
   the AI policy operates over the presented option list.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — Extend `StorylineOption` with `cost`,
  `extraEffect`, and `conditionalSuccessors`; add a `Condition` type.
- `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` — Filter options by affordability, apply cost +
  extra effects, resolve conditional successors; expose a state-aware
  accessibility accessor alongside the pure `getStorylineOptions`.
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — Store the presented/available option list on
  `PendingEventChoice` so indexing and save/load remain stable.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — `resolveEventOption` uses the stored
  presented list; update logging/transcript for cost and extra effects.
- `src/MainStreetEngineScoring.ts` — `decideEventChoice` selects only among
  presented options and accounts for cost/extra-effect deltas.
- `src/scripts/validate-storylines.ts` — Validate cost/condition/effect data and
  conditional successor targets.
- `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` + `schemas/main-street-storyline.schema.json`
  — Represent and validate the new option metadata in the manifest/graph.
- `docs/main-street/storylines.md` — Document the extended option model and
  resolution semantics; update the seam/migration notes.
- `tests/main-street/storyline-model.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/validate-storylines.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/storyline-graph.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/storylines-doc-drift.test.ts` — New/extended coverage.

## Related work

- `MS-0MUB0GFY00001ASV` — **write storylines** (completed epic; parent context).
- `MS-0MUMP93DI0018OGV` — **Storyline model & extraction seam** (completed; the
  generalised `StorylineOption` this extends).
- `MS-0MUMP92O9002772U` — **Storyline behaviour regression harness** (completed;
  the byte-for-byte regression guard).
- `MS-0MUMP944B009PEO6` — **Static validator & npm gate** (completed; the
  validator this extends).
- `MS-0MUMP95IW002ARWJ` — **Storyline authoring helper CLI** (completed).
- `MS-0MUMP94S7008KTI0` — **Storyline graph/manifest export & JSON schema**
  (completed; manifest/schema this extends).
- `MS-0MUPORT1Z000QX8N` — **Support arbitrary callback conditions/successors in
  storyline options** (follow-up, medium priority, `discovered-from` this item).
- Roadmap entry: `docs/main-street/storylines.md` §10.

## Risks

- **Option-index drift.** Filtering options changes the index space; the
  pending-choice list must be frozen at draw time or the UI, AI, and transcript
  can disagree. *Mitigation:* store the presented list on
  `PendingEventChoice` and resolve by index into it.
- **AI divergence.** `decideEventChoice` is currently binary; a generalised
  selector that ignores affordability/cost could pick a hidden option or stall.
  *Mitigation:* route AI through the same presented list; cover with
  regression/Monte Carlo tests.
- **Manifest/schema churn.** Adding optional fields can break the graph export
  or doc-drift test. *Mitigation:* keep new fields optional and update schema,
  exporter, and docs in the same change.
- **Scope creep.** Arbitrary callbacks, CSV authoring, and per-option animation
  are explicitly out of scope; the callback escape hatch is tracked separately
  as `MS-0MUPORT1Z000QX8N`.

---

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Delivery surface.** How far should this change reach?
  - Answer (producer): **A** — extend the in-memory model + engine resolution +
    validator/schema only, programmatically via `registerStorylineOptions`;
    keep the legacy CSV at two-way Accept/Reject. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 — Cost-gated semantics.**
  1. What gates eligibility?
     - Answer (producer): **coins and/or reputation**. Source: interactive reply.
  2. When unaffordable, omitted or shown disabled?
     - Answer (producer): **omitted**. Source: interactive reply.
  3. Is the cost deducted on selection in addition to apply/skip?
     - Answer (producer): **yes**. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 — Conditional successors & per-option extra effects representation.**
  - Answer (producer): **A** — declarative, serialisable data
    (`extraEffect` + ordered `{ when, successorId }` rules with `successorId`
    fallback). Additionally: create a **medium-priority follow-up work item**
    to add arbitrary callbacks. Source: interactive reply. Follow-up created as
    `MS-0MUPORT1Z000QX8N`.

### Assumptions

- No shipped card content is expected to use the new semantics; existing
  legacy/card behaviour must remain byte-for-byte equivalent.
- Because a pending choice blocks all player actions, the set of affordable
  options is stable between draw and resolution; storing the presented list on
  the pending choice makes this explicit and save/load-safe.
- Cost deduction that drops coins or reputation to zero triggers the normal
  loss checks (no special-casing).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUO8B93V002CL06** – Help panel content drifts from PRD milestone 5 (7 sections, >8 lines) (in-progress)
- **MS-0MUOSII720060IZQ** – Implement free market re-roll mechanic (engine + state + bias draw) (blocked)
- **MS-0MUMP94S7008KTI0** – Storyline graph/manifest export & JSON schema (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: accept, acceptance, accessibility, actions, actually (+352 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: accept, acceptance, accessibility, actions, actually (+276 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — matched: accept, acceptance, add, adding, addition (+252 more)

# Intake Brief: Visual storyline authoring editor

**Epic.** Producer decisions (2026-10-01, interactive reply): **Q1 = A (in-repo
local web tool)**; **Q2 = A (epic, decomposed into vertical slices)**;
**Q3 = A (curated form/guided editor)**.

## Problem statement

Storylines can only be authored today by hand-editing `src/card-data.csv` or by
driving the transaction-safe `storyline-author` CLI, and the graph can only be
viewed as a generated Mermaid/JSON artefact. Content designers therefore cannot
*see* the arc they are editing, cannot discover links and dangling targets
visually, and cannot make a guided, validated edit in one place. The seed
roadmap entry (`docs/main-street/storylines.md` §10) calls for a visual
storyline authoring editor that reads `docs/main-street/storyline-manifest.json`,
renders the graph interactively, and writes edits back through the same
transactional, self-validating author operations.

## Users

- **Content designers / producers** — see a storyline's shape at a glance,
  inspect a card's links and metadata, and make guided edits (rename, retarget a
  link, regroup a storyline, add a card) without touching CSV internals.
- **TCE / Main Street developers** — trust that every edit goes through one
  validated, transactional write path and that committed artefacts stay in sync
  with `src/card-data.csv`.
- **Future tooling authors** — reuse an editor/view-model seam that reads the
  manifest rather than re-parsing the CSV.

### Example user stories

- "As a content designer, I want to open a local tool, see the storyline graph
  rendered from the manifest, and click a card to inspect its links, so I can
  understand an arc before changing it."
- "As a content designer, I want to edit a card's name, effect and successor
  links in a form and see a preview plus validation errors, so I cannot write
  a dangling chain."
- "As a content designer, I want the committed graph and manifest regenerated
  automatically after an accepted edit, so the docs never drift from content."
- "As a developer, I want the editor to be a local dev tool that is excluded
  from the game build and reuses the existing author API, so it adds no runtime
  dependency and no second CSV write path."

## Scope areas

### A. Editor host and read-only graph viewer

1. A local web tool launched with `npm run storylines:editor` from the repo
   root, built on the existing Vite/`vite-node` toolchain (no new runtime
   dependency). It is a development tool and must not be included in the game
   build.
2. An interactive, manifest-driven graph view: storyline grouping, choice cards
   distinguished from plain incidents, cycle edges marked, pan/zoom and
   node selection. Read-only in the first slice.

### B. Transactional write bridge

3. A Node-side bridge that exposes the existing author operations
   (`add-card`, `link`, `set-storyline` from `src/scripts/storyline-author.ts`)
   and the validator (`src/scripts/validate-storylines.ts`) to the editor.
4. Every edit is **previewed and validated before writing**; an invalid result
   leaves `src/card-data.csv` untouched and surfaces actionable errors.
5. On an accepted edit, regenerate `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd` and
   `docs/main-street/storyline-manifest.json` via the existing
   `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` generator so the existing drift test stays
   green.
6. Concurrency guard: refuse to overwrite the CSV if it changed on disk outside
   the editor session (content hash / mtime check) and ask the author to reload.

### C. Curated form/guided editing UX

7. Edit an existing card's fields: name, effect text, coin/reputation deltas,
   `hasChoices`, `acceptNextCardId`, `rejectNextCardId`, `storylineId`,
   `storylineTitle`.
8. Add a new card and link it into a storyline through a guided form; discard
   pending (unwritten) changes before committing.

### D. Storyline management, docs and tests

9. Storyline-level operations (create/rename a `storylineId`/`storylineTitle`
   group and reassign member cards) driven through the same author API.
10. Documentation in `docs/main-street/storylines.md` (and the `src/README.md`
    script/column references) covering launch, the viewer, the edit workflow,
    validation and artefact regeneration.
11. Unit tests for the view-model/API bridge and a browser (Playwright) test
    for the viewer and a representative edit round-trip.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Editor launches locally** — `npm run storylines:editor` starts the tool
   from the repo root on the existing Vite/`vite-node` toolchain with no new
   runtime dependency; the command is documented in `docs/main-street/storylines.md`.
   Verified by a test that invokes the entry point (dry/`--help` mode) and asserts
   it exits 0.
2. **Manifest-driven interactive graph** — the editor renders the committed
   manifest (`docs/main-street/storyline-manifest.json`): all nodes and edges
   appear, choice cards are visually distinct, storyline grouping and cycle
   edges are shown, and selecting a node shows its links/metadata. Covered by a
   browser test.
3. **Read-only fidelity** — the editor's view model (nodes, edges, storyline
   ids/titles, cycle flags) matches the committed manifest exactly; verified by
   a unit test that diffs the view model against the manifest and the JSON
   schema.
4. **Curated editing via the author API only** — the editor can edit the fields
   listed in Scope C and add a card; every mutation is routed through
   `src/scripts/storyline-author.ts` (`add-card`/`link`/`set-storyline`). A test
   asserts no editor module writes `src/card-data.csv` except through that
   module, and a round-trip test proves an edited fixture validates.
5. **Preview and validate-before-write** — every edit shows a preview/diff and
   runs the validator before writing; an invalid edit exits non-zero, writes
   nothing, and surfaces the offending card/link. Covered by unit tests against
   valid and deliberately broken edits.
6. **Artefacts regenerated on accepted edit** — after an accepted edit the tool
   regenerates `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd` and
   `docs/main-street/storyline-manifest.json`; `npm run storylines:graph --
   --format json --check` and the doc-drift test pass. Covered by a test.
7. **Concurrency guard** — if `src/card-data.csv` changed on disk since load,
   the editor refuses to write and instructs the author to reload. Covered by a
   unit test.
8. **Game build excluded** — the editor assets/entry are not part of the
   production game bundle; verified by a build/test assertion (e.g. the editor
   entry is not referenced from the game `index.html`/`main.ts` graph).
9. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, `src/README.md`, and any relevant `docs/` entries.
10. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Single write path** — the editor must reuse the existing transactional,
  self-validating author operations; it must not introduce a second way to edit
  `src/card-data.csv`.
- **No new runtime dependency** — reuse the existing Vite/`vite-node`/Vitest/
  Playwright toolchain.
- **Deterministic artefacts** — the manifest/mmd generators must stay
  timestamp-free; the existing drift test must continue to pass.
- **Development tool, not shipped** — the editor must not be pulled into the
  production game build or the packaged Electron app.
- **Backward compatibility** — CSV schema/column order and legacy
  `hasChoices`/accept/reject semantics must be preserved; the C1 regression
  harness must stay green.
- **Preserve designed tension** — the editor is an authoring tool; it must not
  alter player-facing content semantics or reveal escalation content to
  players.
- **UK English** in all UI copy and documentation.
- **Scope guard** — richer option semantics (conditional/cost-gated effects,
  `MS-0MUNB58TK0025CB9`) are out of scope; the editor edits today's two-way
  Accept/Reject CSV model. Record extra opportunities as linked work items.

## Existing state (repo research)

- **Manifest + schema** — `docs/main-street/storyline-manifest.json` (generated,
  deterministic, 5 storyline ids, nodes/edges/cycles) and
  `schemas/main-street-storyline.schema.json` (draft-07, `additionalProperties:
  false`).
- **Graph export** — `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` with
  `npm run storylines:graph -- --format mermaid|json` and a `--check` drift
  guard; committed `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd`.
- **Transactional author API** — `src/scripts/storyline-author.ts` (CLI
  `npm run storylines:author`, `add-card`/`link`/`set-storyline`): builds the
  edited CSV in memory, loads it through the typed model and validates **before**
  writing; `--dry-run` and `--csv <path>` supported.
- **Validator** — `src/scripts/validate-storylines.ts` (`validateStorylines`,
  `formatStorylineReport`), cycles informational, `--fail-on-cycle` opt-in.
- **Model/seam** — `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` (`compileStorylineFromEvent`,
  `getStorylineOptions`, `registerStorylineOptions`, `resolveStorylineOption`,
  `pushChainCard`); CSV authoring keeps the two-way representation.
- **Stack** — Vite + Phaser + Electron; scripts run under `vite-node` because
  the card model imports `src/card-data.csv` through Vite's `?raw` query.
- **Gap** — no interactive editor; the only graph view is the static generated
  Mermaid/JSON; nobody can edit through a UI. Even the strongest surrounding
  visualisation item (`MS-0MUNB54KU005084C`) only renders the committed `.mmd`
  to SVG in the docs build.

## Desired change

1. **Host a local editor** — `npm run storylines:editor` serves an in-repo dev
   page backed by a small Node-side API bridge over the author/validator/graph
   modules.
2. **Interactive viewer** — render the manifest graph with storyline grouping,
   choice/plain distinction, cycle marking, pan/zoom/select.
3. **Guided editing** — edit card fields and add/relink cards through forms that
   preview the diff and validate before write.
4. **Stay in sync** — regenerate the committed mmd/manifest after accepted edits
   and guard against concurrent external CSV edits.
5. **Document and test** — authoring walkthrough for the editor, unit tests for
   the bridge/view-model and a browser round-trip test.

**Recommended slice order for planning** (epic, per Q2 = A): (S1) host +
read-only viewer; (S2) write bridge + preview/validate; (S3) curated edit forms;
(S4) storyline management + docs/tests polish. The `plan` skill will formalise
the children and dependencies.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scripts/storyline-editor-cli.ts` — **new** entry point (`vite-node`).
- `src/scripts/storyline-editor-server.ts` (or a Vite dev-server plugin) —
  **new** host + API bridge.
- `src/scripts/storyline-editor-api.ts` — **new** thin wrapper over
  `storyline-author.ts`, `validate-storylines.ts`, `storyline-graph.ts`.
- `src/tools/storyline-editor/` (or `tools/storyline-editor/`) — **new** editor
  UI (HTML entry + TS view-model/graph rendering).
- `package.json` — add the `storylines:editor` script.
- `docs/main-street/storylines.md` — **edit** tooling/authoring sections.
- `src/README.md` — **edit** script and CSV-column references.
- `tests/main-street/storyline-editor.test.ts` — **new** bridge/view-model tests.
- `tests/main-street/storyline-editor.browser.test.ts` — **new** Playwright UI test.
- `docs/main-street/storyline-manifest.json`, `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd`
  — generated artefacts (regenerated on accepted edits).

## Related work

- **MS-0MUB0GFY00001ASV** — "write storylines" (epic, completed/in_review) — the
  parent that shipped the validator, graph/manifest export and authoring helper
  this editor builds on; its roadmap entry in
  `docs/main-street/storylines.md` §10 is the seed for this work item.
- **MS-0MUMP95IW002ARWJ** — "Storyline authoring helper CLI" (completed) — the
  transactional write API the editor wraps.
- **MS-0MUMP94S7008KTI0** — "Storyline graph/manifest export & JSON schema"
  (completed) — the manifest/schema/generator the viewer reads.
- **MS-0MUMP944B009PEO6** — "Static validator & npm gate" (completed) — the
  validation feedback surfaced in the editor.
- **MS-0MUMP92O9002772U** — "Storyline behaviour regression harness" (completed)
  — must stay green after editor changes.
- **MS-0MUNB54KU005084C** — "Render the storyline graph (Mermaid to SVG) in the
  docs build" (in-progress) — adjacent read-only visualisation; potential
  overlap in rendering conventions.
- **MS-0MUNB58TK0025CB9** — "Extend storyline options with conditional and
  cost-gated effects" (open) — future option model; explicitly out of scope here,
  but the editor's form model should not preclude it.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope risk (epic)** — "visual editor" can balloon into a full graph editor;
  *mitigation:* slice order (viewer → bridge → forms → management) and keep
  direct-manipulation graph editing out of the accepted first increments.
- **Write-path risk** — a browser UI could grow its own CSV writer;
  *mitigation:* AC4 enforces the author-API-only path with a test.
- **Concurrency risk** — external CSV edits during an editor session could be
  overwritten; *mitigation:* AC7 hash/mtime guard.
- **Build-leak risk** — the editor entry could be bundled into the game;
  *mitigation:* AC8 build exclusion test.
- **`?raw` import constraint** — the card model imports the CSV via Vite `?raw`,
  so the bridge must run under `vite-node`/Vite middleware rather than plain
  Node; *mitigation:* the host builds on the existing toolchain (Q1 = A).
- **Assumption** — "storylines" means the Main Street incident event-chain
  system; no other storyline implementation exists in the repo.
- **Assumption** — the editor is a local developer/content tool; hostability
  outside a repo checkout is not required.
- **Assumption** — the editor's first increments target the shipped two-way
  Accept/Reject CSV model; multi-way/programmatic options remain out of scope.
- **Assumption** — CHANGELOG is managed by the release pipeline and is out of
  scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

### Answered (producer, round 1 — 2026-10-01, interactive reply)

- **Q1 — Delivery form / host.** Where should the editor live and how is it
  launched? Options: (A) in-repo local web tool; (B) in-game developer overlay;
  (C) standalone Electron tool. **Recommended:** (A). **Final accepted answer:
  A — in-repo local web tool** launched with `npm run storylines:editor`, built
  on the existing Vite/`vite-node` toolchain and writing only through the
  existing author API. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 — Work-item shape & first increment.** Options: (A) epic decomposed into
  vertical slices; (B) single feature; (C) read-only MVP only.
  **Recommended:** (A). **Final accepted answer: A — epic**, decomposed into
  vertical slices (viewer → write bridge → edit forms → storyline management +
  docs/tests). The work item's `issueType` was set to `epic`. Source:
  interactive reply.
- **Q3 — Editing interaction model.** Options: (A) curated form/guided editor;
  (B) direct-manipulation graph editor; (C) both (form first, graph later).
  **Recommended:** (A). **Final accepted answer: A — curated form/guided
  editor**, with diff/preview and validate-before-write; no free-form canvas
  manipulation. Source: interactive reply.

### Answered (repo research — no interactive reply needed)

- **Q0 — Write path.** The editor must use the existing transactional author
  API (`src/scripts/storyline-author.ts`: `add-card`/`link`/`set-storyline`)
  and must not add a second CSV edit path. Evidence: the author module already
  validates in memory before writing; the seed states "write edits back through
  the same transactional, self-validating author operations".
- **Q0b — Artefacts.** After an accepted edit, regenerate
  `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd` and
  `docs/main-street/storyline-manifest.json` via
  `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts`; the existing `--check` drift guard and
  doc-drift test must pass. Evidence: `docs/main-street/storylines.md` §5/§7.
- **Q0c — Stack constraint.** The editor host must run under Vite/`vite-node`
  because the card model imports `src/card-data.csv` through Vite's `?raw`
  query. Evidence: the `storyline-author`/`storyline-graph`/`validate-storylines`
  CLIs are all `vite-node` entry points.

### Open questions

- None. All blocking questions are answered (Q1–Q3, producer); the epic scope
  and slice order are set above.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUDYQQ2E00913QN** – Synergy tooltop (completed)
- **MS-0MUO7CPH3003TXFI** – Reduce time upcoming event is shown (blocked)
- **MS-0MUMO3BDE000QDXJ** – Test review: apply transferred clean-ups from the core test-suite audit (in-progress)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: author, authoring, back, cli, command (+33 more)
- `docs/main-street/storylines.md` — matched: author, authoring, back, command, deferred (+25 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: author, back, cli, command, deferred (+24 more)

# Extend the StorylineOption model with new optional fields

## Summary

Add `cost`, `extraEffect`, and `conditionalSuccessors` to the `StorylineOption` interface in `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts`, plus a new `Condition` type. This is the foundational model change — all downstream features depend on it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Model extension.** `StorylineOption` gains optional `cost: { coins?: number; reputation?: number }`, `extraEffect: { coins?: number; reputation?: number }`, and `conditionalSuccessors: readonly Condition[]` fields. All three are optional; omitting all preserves current behaviour.
- **Condition type.** A new `Condition` type is defined: `{ field: 'coins' | 'reputation'; op: '>=' | '<=' | '>' | '<' | '=='; value: number }`.
- **Backwards compatibility.** All existing `StorylineOption` usages compile without error. No breaking changes to any interface or API.
- **No shipped content uses new fields.** Existing CSV cards are unaffected.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — Extend `StorylineOption`, add `Condition` type.

## Deliverables

- Updated type definitions with JSDoc.
- All existing usages compile without error.
- Type-only change — no runtime logic.

## Dependencies

None.

## Goal

Establish the shared test/verification foundation for the visual storyline
editor so every later feature can be driven test-first. This task writes
**test infrastructure only** — no editor feature code.

## Context

The editor is a dev tool launched under Vite/`vite-node`; the card model
imports `src/card-data.csv` through Vite's `?raw` query, so bridge tests must
run through the same toolchain. Repo test facts:

- `npm test` runs `vitest run --project unit` (Vitest; `tests/**/*.test.ts`,
  excluding `*.browser.test.ts`).
- Browser tests (`tests/**/*.browser.test.ts`) run through Vitest browser mode
  with the Playwright chromium provider (`@vitest/browser`, `playwright` are
  existing devDependencies) — project wiring lives with the launcher
  distribution, so a dev page (not a Phaser scene) needs explicit wiring.
- `ajv` is an existing devDependency and is used for JSON schema validation.
- The root `vite.config.ts` is **auto-generated** by
  `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`; do not hand-edit it — use a dedicated
  editor config file.

## Scope

- Fixture helper that copies `src/card-data.csv`,
  `docs/main-street/storyline-manifest.json` and
  `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd` into an isolated temp directory and
  returns the paths, so edit tests never mutate committed files.
- A reusable write-path guard helper: scans editor source files and asserts no
  module writes `src/card-data.csv` except through `src/scripts/storyline-author.ts`
  (tolerant of editor modules not existing yet).
- A manifest schema guard test: committed manifest validates against
  `schemas/main-street-storyline.schema.json` using `ajv`.
- A browser-test harness decision/spike: determine and wire how the editor dev
  page is driven in Vitest browser mode (or justify an alternative), with a
  placeholder test that passes. Record the decision in a comment on this item.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A fixture helper returns isolated temp copies of the CSV/manifest/mmd, and a
  test asserts the committed originals are byte-identical afterwards.
- The write-path guard helper is exercised by a test and would fail if an
  editor module wrote the CSV directly (proven with a synthetic negative case).
- The committed manifest validates against the JSON schema in a unit test using
  the existing `ajv` devDependency.
- The browser-test path for a non-Phaser dev page is decided, wired and
  documented; a placeholder browser test passes without adding a runtime
  dependency.
- `npm test` and the browser suite run the new harness green.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `tests/main-street/storyline-editor/fixtures.ts` — **new** temp-copy helper.
- `tests/main-street/storyline-editor/fixtures.test.ts` — **new** helper test.
- `tests/main-street/storyline-editor/write-path-guard.ts` — **new** reusable static guard.
- `tests/main-street/storyline-editor/write-path-guard.test.ts` — **new**.

- `vite.editor.config.ts` — **new** dedicated editor/harness config (not the auto-generated `./vite.config.ts`).

## Deliverables

  browser-test path, harness smoke coverage.

# Intake brief — Grand Opening provides bonus for each synergy business (MS-0MV8KSPFK006HTXG)

## Headline

Grand Opening Sale currently pays a fixed bonus per **Commerce** business; it should pay per business sharing the synergy of the business opened (placed) on that same turn, so the reward tracks the player's placement rather than a hard-coded sector.

## Problem statement

`evt-grand-opening` (Grand Opening Sale, cost 300, Investment) is defined in `card-data.csv` as a `SpecificSynergy` event with a static `targetSynergy: Commerce` and `coinDelta: 450` — i.e. it always rewards `450 × (Commerce businesses on the grid)` (CG-0MTIOCBH400970OB added a same-turn placement gate requiring a business/community-space to be placed that turn). The fixed Commerce target makes the card's payoff unrelated to what the player actually opened: a player who places a non-Commerce business still gets rewarded solely for their Commerce holdings.

## Users / user stories

- **Player** — "As a player who just opened a Café (Food) next to my Bakery, I want Grand Opening Sale to pay off my Food businesses, because I built around that placement."
- **AI opponent (competitive)** — "As the AI, I want event-value estimates to match the actual dynamic payout so I don't over- or under-value Grand Opening Sale."

## Desired change

- On resolution, Grand Opening Sale's bonus applies to **each grid business/community-space sharing the synergy of the card placed (opened) this turn** — the placement that armed the gate — instead of the static `Commerce` target.
- The placement paths must record the placed card's synergy type(s) for the turn; the state machinery (week-start reset, serialisation/backfill, undo snapshot) must carry it.
- Both single-player and competitive resolution, plus AI/projection value paths and animation attribution, must use the same dynamic synergy so projections and payouts never diverge.
- Card copy/docs updated so the effect text no longer claims "from a Commerce promotion".

## Acceptance Criteria (measurable)

1. Play `evt-grand-opening` in a turn where a non-Commerce business (e.g. Food) was placed: coins increase by `450 × (number of grid cards sharing that placed business's synergy)`, and Commerce businesses are **not** counted unless they also share the placed synergy.
2. Placing a card with multiple synergy types (e.g. `Food|Culture`) rewards any grid card sharing **any** of the placed card's synergy types (union semantics, consistent with existing `synergyTypes.some()` matching).
3. Placing a community space (which already arms the gate, per the same-turn gate test) drives the synergy selection symmetrically with business placements.
4. Single-player (`resolveEvent`) and competitive (`applyCompetitiveEventEffects` / `computeOwnerEventDeltas`), the AI/projection helpers (`projectEventCoinDelta`, `computeCompetitiveEventValue`), and per-slot animation attribution (`MainStreetAdjacencyScoring`) all resolve the same dynamic synergy for the event — no divergence between projection and payout.
5. State lifecycle: the recorded placed synergy resets at week start, survives save/load with legacy backfill, and is included in the undo snapshot so undoing a placement restores the pre-placement synergy.
6. Card copy and docs updated: `card-data.csv` `effect` text, `docs/game/card-catalog.md`, and `docs/dev/analysis/community-space-event-repricing.md` no longer describe a fixed Commerce promotion.
7. Tests: new/extended unit coverage for dynamic synergy resolution (single-player and competitive), union matching, community-space placements, lifecycle (reset/backfill/undo), and AI/competitive projection parity. Full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- Do not remove or relax the existing same-turn placement gate (CG-0MTIOCBH400970OB) — this item extends its payoff semantics only.
- Keep the card's static `targetSynergy: Commerce` in `card-data.csv` **unless** the implementer can verify that removing it does not degrade market-refill relevance (`isMarketCardRelevant`) and tooltip consumers; minimal-change default is a resolution-time override keyed on `evt-grand-opening`.
- Integer-only payouts (CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6): `450 × count` stays integer by construction.
- CHANGELOG.md is excluded — managed by the ship release pipeline.

## Existing state

- `src/card-data.csv` row 46: `event,evt-grand-opening,...,SpecificSynergy,Commerce,450,...` effect "+450 coins from a Commerce promotion."
- `businessPlacedThisTurn?: boolean` gate field: `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` (~529–534), armed in `purchaseBusiness` (`MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts` ~362), `playBusinessFromHand` (`MainStreetMarketHand.ts` ~148), `buyAndPlaceBusiness` (`MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` ~770), reset at week start (`MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts` ~57), serialised/backfilled (`MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` ~359), undo-snapshotted (`MainStreetCommands.ts`).
- Resolution: `SpecificSynergy` counts `streetGrid` cards whose `synergyTypes` include `event.targetSynergy` in `resolveEvent` (`MainStreetEngineEvents.ts` ~100), `applyCompetitiveEventEffects` (~301), `computeOwnerEventDeltas` (~477); AI/competitive projections in `MainStreetEngineScoring.ts` `projectEventCoinDelta` (~140) and `MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` `computeCompetitiveEventValue` (~2210); per-slot animation attribution in `MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` (~972).
- Tests: `tests/main-street/grand-opening-same-turn-gate.test.ts` (gate lifecycle), `tests/main-street/event-card-tooltip-info.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/piggyback-eligibility.test.ts` (lists `evt-grand-opening` as piggybackable).

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — new state field recording the placed card's synergy types this turn (e.g. `placedBusinessSynergiesThisTurn?: SynergyType[]`), adjacent to `businessPlacedThisTurn`.
- `src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts` / `src/MainStreetMarketHand.ts` / `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` — set the new field in each of the three placement paths.
- `src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts` — reset the new field alongside `businessPlacedThisTurn`.
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` / `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts` / `src/MainStreetCommands.ts` — serialise, legacy backfill, and undo snapshot for the new field.
- `src/MainStreetEngineEvents.ts` — dynamic synergy resolution in `resolveEvent`, `applyCompetitiveEventEffects`, `computeOwnerEventDeltas`.
- `src/MainStreetEngineScoring.ts` / `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — mirror dynamic resolution in `projectEventCoinDelta` / `computeCompetitiveEventValue` (and check `scoreEventAction`).
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` — per-slot animation attribution uses the dynamic synergy.
- `src/card-data.csv` / `docs/game/card-catalog.md` / `docs/dev/analysis/community-space-event-repricing.md` — effect copy + documentation.
- `tests/main-street/grand-opening-dynamic-synergy.test.ts` (new) + updates to `grand-opening-same-turn-gate.test.ts` and `event-card-tooltip-info.test.ts`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Divergence risk**: the payout path (`resolveEvent` / competitive per-owner math) and the AI/projection paths (`projectEventCoinDelta`, `computeCompetitiveEventValue`, piggyback projection, animation attribution) share the `targetSynergy` lookup — if only the payout path is updated, the AI will mis-value the card. Mitigation: a single shared dynamic-synergy resolver used by every path; AC 4 + projection-parity tests.
- **Piggyback interplay** (competitive, `evt-grand-opening` is piggybackable): piggyback reward projections must reflect the dynamic payout too — include in AC 4/7 coverage.
- **Scope-creep risk**: predictive/strategy re-tuning of Grand Opening's cost/coinDelta in light of the dynamic target is **out of scope** here; record any rebalancing as a new linked work item.
- **Assumption**: union synergy matching for multi-synergy cards, community-space placements drive selection, most-recent placement wins — recorded in the Appendix; producer confirmation requested.

## Related work

- MS-0MUR9IN7L0004TO5 — Re-price community spaces and events relative to slower business payback (related balance context)
- MS-0MUX8J9KJ005ZKDW — AI uses community space cards too much (AI valuation context)
- MS-0MUWKG6NS006OG2D — Community Garden should be Entertainment (synergy data context)
- CG-0MTIOCBH400970OB — Grand Opening Sale same-turn placement gate (commit `a3e2b5de`; basis for this change)
- Duplicate check performed — no overlapping open/completed item found.

---

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No blocking producer questions were required — the seed intent ("bonus for each business with the same synergy as the one opened on that turn") is specific, and the remaining decisions follow from repo mechanics and precedent. Records (idempotent; do not duplicate on re-run):

- Q: Dynamic synergy should be union or exact for multi-synergy placed cards? — **Answer (research, agent-recommended):** union — any grid card sharing any of the placed card's `synergyTypes` counts; consistent with existing `synergyTypes.some()`/`.includes()` matching in `MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` and `isMarketCardRelevant`. Source: repo matching code; optional producer confirmation.
- Q: Does a community-space placement drive the synergy (it already arms the gate)? — **Answer (research, agent-recommended):** yes, symmetric with the gate (CG-0MTIOCBH400970OB test arms on "business (or community-space)"). Source: existing gate behaviour + test file.
- Q: Which placement counts if a player places multiple cards in one turn? — **Answer (research, agent-recommended):** the most recent placement (last placement wins), matching conventional "the one opened" reading; single-action turns make collisions rare. Source: default `actionsRemaining` = 1.
- Q: Should the static `targetSynergy: Commerce` row field be removed from CSV? — **Answer (research, agent-recommended):** no — keep it as the static field; override dynamically at resolution keyed on `evt-grand-opening`, to avoid silent changes to market-refill relevance (`isMarketCardRelevant`) and tooltip consumers. Source: `MainStreetStateSetup.ts` relevance logic, tooltip tests.

# Feature 3: AI/projection parity

## Summary
Mirror the dynamic synergy in AI value/projection paths so projections never diverge from the actual payout: `projectEventCoinDelta`, `countOwnSynergyMatches` callers, `scoreEventAction`, `computeCompetitiveEventValue`, `MainStreetAdjacencyScoring` animation attribution, and piggyback projections.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `projectEventCoinDelta` for `evt-grand-opening` counts grid cards sharing the placed synergies (per current state), not static Commerce.
2. Competitive AI path: `computeCompetitiveEventValue` and any `scoreEventAction` usage compute the dynamic (per-owner) value.
3. Piggyback reward projections (competitive grand-opening is piggybackable) reflect the dynamic payout.
4. `MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` per-slot animation attribution flags the same dynamic-match slots.
5. A shared resolver/helper is used by all paths so projection and payout can never diverge (single source of truth).

## Dependencies
Depends on Feature 2 resolution (MS-0MVCS7LIA003J2SM).

A bare Condition cannot determine a successor, so I implemented the parent's authoritative shape: `conditionalSuccessors?: readonly ConditionalSuccessor[]` where ConditionalSuccessor = { when: Condition; successorId: string }. This is presentational in this item (type-only) and unblocks the resolution child. Cost/extraEffect share the StorylineResourceDelta type (coins?/reputation?).

## AC4 — browser-test harness decision (recorded)

**Decision: Vitest browser mode + Playwright chromium; drive the editor dev page by importing its modules and mounting them into a DOM container.**

The editor dev page is a **non-Phaser** Vite page (root `src/tools/storyline-editor/`, served by the dedicated `vite.editor.config.ts`). It is covered by the existing `browser` project in `vite.config.ts` (`include: ['tests/**/*.browser.test.ts']`, provider `playwright`, chromium, headless). Browser tests **import the editor's modules into the browser context and mount them into a DOM container** — exactly the pattern the existing scene browser tests use (`bootGame()` imports `createMainStreetGame` and attaches it to `#game-container`).

### Why this over a separate HTTP-server fence

- No new runtime dependency: reuses the already-wired `@vitest/browser` + `playwright` devDependencies.
- No separate dev server / port lifecycle to orchestrate inside the test run — deterministic and hermetic.
- The future read-only viewer slice (F1) renders into the same container seam.

### Wiring

- Placeholder test: `tests/main-street/storyline-editor/harness.browser.test.ts` — loads the committed manifest (`docs/dev/assets/storyline-manifest.json`) through the Vite transform in the browser and asserts the committed storyline ids render to the DOM. This proves the page/data-loading seam before any editor module exists.
- Wired into the browser suite via `.pi/test-config.json` `suiteCommands` (appended to the existing browser command so a single chromium launch runs both files).
- Shared manifest types added at `tests/main-street/storyline-editor/manifest-types.ts` so the harness, the schema guard and the future view model agree on one contract.
